feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization support trust and show increasing responsibility.  
- Strong scope and impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, analytics stack, studio buildout, and cross-channel leadership all add weight.  
- Good positioning for target roles: summary, competencies, and technical skills consistently reinforce digital strategy, CMS modernization, and mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Add more outcome-based metrics beyond scale: include results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign outcomes.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); keep hyphenation consistent (“cross-channel/multi-channel,” “organization-wide”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with sharper positioning and cleaner phrasing would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more concise phrase like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, editorial workflows, and digital systems that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “advocacy messaging” overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with channel lists since those are detailed in Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, senior-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Web platform modernization,” “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items; suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial systems, workflow design & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently; “cross-functional” is cleaner than “cross-department.”
- Consider dropping one lower-priority item if space is tight; nine competencies feels slightly crowded.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with Topline Skills and Technical + IT; “editorial systems & governance” may be more distinctive.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scope, and the most distinctive elements so it adds new value beyond your NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + audience: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, content operations, and enterprise web modernization across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: emphasize what changed, e.g., “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance to improve cross-team coordination and publishing efficiency.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits, while providing front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but add measurable scope if possible: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with NACo Director role; in this item, stress consulting impact, current modernization work, and AI/search.
- “Web, email, social, multimedia” already appears elsewhere; avoid repeating channel lists in multiple bullets.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be stronger if you tighten the opening and make outcomes more explicit. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and enterprise impact rather than listing every channel.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper summary: “Led NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national association serving county officials.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Directed redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, engagement lifts, production savings, faster reporting, reduced vendor spend, or improved publishing efficiency.
- Tighten wording: combine “clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems” into one results-oriented bullet tied to consistency, speed, or accountability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier Associate Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with prior multimedia bullets; stress that this was the first in-house broadcast studio and its organizational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later NACo role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth before promotion to Director.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; clarify what was new here (scale, ownership, or formalization).

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to enterprise-scale leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider adding one scale cue if your format allows, e.g., “enterprise web and communications ecosystems” or “multi-stakeholder publishing environments.”
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect your recent leadership in systems, workflows, and governance.
- Keep terminology aligned with recent roles: “cross-channel” and “governance” match the strongest experience evidence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “multi-channel communications leadership” repeat ideas already stated in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is supported, but avoid repeating “policy communication” language used elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation; move older/less central tools later.
- Tighten wording: change “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)” unless jQuery is specifically required for target roles.
- If space allows, add light scope language: “enterprise CMS” or “large public-facing web platforms” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Most platform/tool names duplicate “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and less exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant analytics stack for recent leadership roles, but this item reads like a tool list rather than a value statement. It would be stronger if grouped around decision-making impact and trimmed to avoid overlap with work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g.: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework development, executive reporting, SEO and performance analysis.”
- Put the most marketable/strategic terms first: analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, then tools.
- Consider tightening “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Board/executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If accurate, add one higher-level term such as “measurement strategy” or “conversion/performance optimization” to show application, not just platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; keep the CV item concise and let the experience bullet carry the proof.
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and aligned to recent leadership-level work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize scope: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event production • PTZ camera and multi-camera studio systems • Studio buildout and operations • Virtual event execution**
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **Built and operated an in-house broadcast studio supporting advocacy programming and recurring live content**
- Keep terms consistent with experience bullets; use either **livestream** or **live event** language throughout, not both repeatedly

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies: **Multimedia & live event production**; consider removing that broader competency or narrowing one of the two
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already implied by NACo experience, so avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it either more specific to platform depth/recent use or trim it to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: “Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: put Drupal first and consider grouping lesser-used tools last.
- Consider replacing “GitHub Pages” with a more business-relevant qualifier only if you’ve used it meaningfully, e.g. “GitHub Pages (lightweight static sites)”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “CMS platforms” or “Web Platforms & CMS,” not both.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it without adding context or proficiency.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied execution, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling separately: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add a brief qualifier tied to recent work: “for Drupal-based sites, campaign microsites, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more contemporary

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; either shorten this item or make Topline Skills more strategic and this section more tool-specific
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” already appear elsewhere, so avoid repeating both in identical wording across sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” language already present in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: **Airtable (workflow/database systems)**, **Power Automate & Zapier (process automation)**, **Jira/Asana/Trello (editorial and project tracking)**
- Consider trimming older/lower-signal tools like **Basecamp** if you need space for more current, higher-value platforms

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates **“Workflow automation”** and **“Airtable systems”** in Topline Skills; keep this version tool-focused and let Topline Skills carry the strategic framing
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; include them only if they support a broader collaboration-systems narrative

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant and current, but it reads as a bare vendor list rather than showing level of use or strategic ownership. It should better signal enterprise email/engagement capability without repeating newsletter work already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength cue: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter delivery, audience segmentation, and member engagement platforms**
- If space allows, combine into one line: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email automation, segmentation, and member engagement**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding newsletter audience size or campaign management details here; those are already covered in NACo experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language, which is already strong in the summary and core competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team build-out, early platform/content production ownership, and any concrete scale/results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add scope/outcomes where possible: website refresh size/traffic, livestream frequency/audience, weekly video cadence, or process improvements (faster publishing, more consistent output, reduced vendor reliance).
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables such as “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy videos, and web/social content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored one junior team member.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Tighten the scope and emphasize initiative, ownership, and any outputs or audiences if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast,” then add end-to-end ownership.
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business support language tied to programs/policy teams.
- Trim “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” into a more active, specific clause.
- Example rewrite: “Supported county innovation and research initiatives for NACo program and policy teams, translating findings into digital and multimedia content. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here if later NACo roles already show stronger video/digital leadership; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and program/policy support.
- “Digital content production” may overlap with the 2015–2018 role unless you specify format or purpose.
